$comment: The world's values: Schwartz's ten basic values, defining goals paraphrased from Schwartz, S. H. (2012), An Overview of the Schwartz Theory of Basic Values, Online Readings in Psychology and Culture 2(1).

importance.0: does not matter to this person
importance.4: central to who this person is

values.description: independent thought and action: choosing your own course, creating, exploring
excitement, novelty and challenge in life
personal success through showing competence by the standards of those around you
status and prestige, control or dominance over people and resources
safety, harmony and stability of your society, your relationships and yourself
restraint of actions and impulses likely to upset or harm others or break social expectations
respect for and commitment to the customs and ideas your culture or faith provides
preserving and enhancing the welfare of the people close to you
understanding, tolerance and protection for the welfare of all people and of nature
